key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine removes excess tin and reconstructs tin-rich perovskite surfaces, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to examine iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Integrate treated absorbers with C60 electron-extraction layers in methylammonium-free solar cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations indicating that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or scalability of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
